title: Implement Assembler: collect parts, detect gaps, verify CRC32, finish
description:
Core implementation of yencoding-multi.

Assembler internals:
- total_size: u64 -- from =ybegin size= of any part (all parts must agree; mismatch -> OutOfRange)
- parts: Vec<(Range<u64>, Vec<u8>)> -- 0-based ranges and decoded data, sorted by start
- whole_file_crc32: Option<u32> -- from =yend crc32= when present

add_part(part: DecodedPart):
- Convert 1-based begin/end from DecodedPart to 0-based Range<u64>: range = (begin-1)..(end)
- Verify range is within 0..total_size; else Err(OutOfRange)
- Check for overlap with existing parts; else Err(OverlappingPart)
- Store (range, part.data)
- If part.data.len() != (end - begin + 1) as usize: this is a corrupt part -- decide: store anyway with is_truncated flag, or Err? Recommendation: store with a warning in AssemblyError::TruncatedPart

missing_ranges() -> Vec<Range<u64>>:
- Compute the complement of covered ranges within 0..total_size
- Sorted by start, non-overlapping

is_complete() -> bool:
- missing_ranges().is_empty()

finish(self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, AssemblyError>:
- If !is_complete(): Err(Incomplete { missing: missing_ranges() })
- Allocate Vec<u8> of total_size
- Write each part's data to its offset (copy_from_slice)
- If whole_file_crc32 is Some: compute CRC32 of assembled bytes, verify
- Return Ok(assembled)

Tests:
- 3-part file: add all 3 in order, finish -> correct bytes
- 3-part file: add out of order (3, 1, 2), finish -> same correct bytes
- Missing part 2: is_complete() = false, missing_ranges() = [correct range]
- Overlapping parts: Err(OverlappingPart)
- Out-of-range part: Err(OutOfRange)
- CRC32 mismatch on finish: Err(CrcMismatch)
- Test oracle: assemble known byte patterns split into known ranges; verify reassembled output exactly
